messages:
Maria: Quick thought - do we standardize internal S2S APIs on gRPC+protobufs or keep JSON/REST for most things? Thinking about typed SDKs, telemetry, rollout UX.
Jon: +1 for gRPC for core services. Strong typing + smaller wire size. But browser edge is harder.
Elaine: We already have a mash of styles. Full gRPC everywhere is a big infra lift and a migration headache.
Kevin: Performance wins for proto, and streaming RPCs help for long-lived inference streams. Also simpler backpressure.
Maria: Two patterns on the table:
- "Proto-first": gRPC internal, use gRPC-Web/Envoy at the edge.
- "Hybrid": Keep HTTP/JSON for edge; translate to proto internally (gateway/broker).
Jon: Gateway-transcoding is appealing but Envoy's grpc_json_transcoder forces proto shapes to match REST ergonomics. It leaks edge concerns into protos.
Elaine: Also: telemetry and auth headers get messy across translation. We need strict propagation rules in the gateway (trace, request-id, tenant).
Kevin: PoC envoy snippet we used: ```
http_filters:
- name: envoy.filters.http.grpc_json_transcoder
  typed_config:
    "@type": type.googleapis.com/envoy.extensions.filters.http.grpc_json_transcoder.v3.GrpcJsonTranscoder
    proto_descriptor: "/etc/protos/descriptor.pb"
    services: ["redwood.internal.Inference"]
```
Elaine: That worked but updating descriptor.pb on every proto change was a pain. It made canaries fraught.
Maria: How do we canary proto changes? With REST we do path or header versioning. Protos can be additive but renames/removals break clients.
Jon: We can rely on additive-safe changes + gateway route weights for canarying. Also generate compatibility tests for backward/forward compatibility on CI.
Kevin: Another option: thin broker layer. Edge accepts JSON, broker translates to protobuf and calls internal gRPC. Pros: keeps edge simple, lets internal services be proto-first. Cons: broker is a critical piece for quotas/tracing and becomes operationally heavy.
Elaine: Central broker simplifies observability - one place to enforce quotas, inject trace ids, and tag tenant info. But it increases latency and a single point to scale.
Maria: For quotas and per-tenant routing we probably need enforcement at the gateway boundary regardless of payload format. Need token-level checks there.
Jon: Telemetry note: ensure trace id in gRPC metadata and HTTP headers. Add middleware to fill/generate if missing. Also surface failures in transcoding to SLO dashboards.
Kevin: For typed clients: generate SDKs from protos for hot-path services (inference, routing, auth). Leave low-ROI services as JSON.
Elaine: So pragmatic hybrid: proto-first for core infra, JSON at edge, broker or Envoy translation where needed. Document the migration path and compatibility rules.
Maria: Action items:
- Kevin: RFC comparing broker vs Envoy transcoding (tradeoffs + perf) - due next Wed.
- Jon: implement trace/header passthrough tests in gateway this sprint.
- Elaine: inventory top ~12 services and propose proto-first candidates.
- Maria: coordinate SRE on rollout runbook for descriptor regeneration and canaries.
sre-bot: deploy-bot: completed canary rollout for gateway v2 at 1951237680 :white_check_mark:
Jon: Nice.
Maria: Thanks everyone, will sync Friday with RFC draft if ready.
